title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
summary: On a 2D plane, place n stones at integer coordinates with each point holding at most one stone.
statement: On a 2D plane, place n stones at integer coordinates with each point holding at most one stone. A stone can be removed if it aligns with another unremoved stone in the same row or column. Given an array of stone coordinates, determine the maximum number of stones that can be removed.
constraints: A stone can be removed while another stone shares its row or column.
hints: Within each connected row/column component, all but one stone can be removed.
Union row vertices with separately tagged column vertices.
Count distinct component roots among stones and return stones-components.
Connectivity supplies a removal order, while one final stone per component must remain.
editorial: Connectivity supplies a removal order, while one final stone per component must remain.

tests.explanation: All six stones form one connected component, so five can be removed.
The only stone has no partner and cannot be removed.
